card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent gets whole-patch approval but not hunk-level edits, conflicts and schema parity. Buckets: whole approve and reject, per-hunk, modified hunks, conflict, schema. A weaker model fails on protocol plumbing.
card.cheat: Auto-approving everything. Hidden clients reject and modify hunks, and the final bytes are checked.
card.grading: Hidden protocol tests act as a scripted client over stdio JSON-RPC against a mock model. They check message shapes, the final file contents after partial approvals, and conflict outcomes. Reward is the fraction passed, with the existing app-server tests as a gate.
card.reference: Written by us: about 1600 lines of Rust across the protocol types, the patch application and the server handlers. It scores 1.
card.task: /app ships a snapshot of the Rust workspace at the base. The agent adds to the app-server protocol a request and response flow in which proposed file edits are sent to the client as structured diffs. The client can approve, reject or modify each hunk, and the decision is applied back to the patch before it is run. It also covers per-hunk partial approval, conflict detection with edits made by the editor in the meantime, and schema generation.

v1.summary: The Apache-2.0 repo, the open issue #2998 and the rust-v0.163.0 tag all check out, but upstream already has a v2 file-change approval RPC (PR #6760, follow-up #8451), so the base must be stripped and the per-hunk flow is not found in public sources. The Rust build was never probed (the smoke probe ran a node check at a different commit), so the build cost is unknown and the seed should go to a spike with the conditions above before any further investment.
